- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Roman Empire officially fell on 4 September 476 CE.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Germanic king Odoacer deposed the last Roman Emperor, Romulus Augustus, marking the formal end of the Western Roman Empire.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The fall of the Roman Empire was a gradual process that occurred over several centuries.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The empire began to decline in the 2nd and 3rd centuries CE due to a combination of internal decay and external pressures.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] By the 5th century CE, the empire had been divided into two parts: the Western Roman Empire and the Eastern Roman Empire.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Western Roman Empire faced significant challenges, including invasions by barbarian tribes, economic troubles, and political instability.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Some sources estimate that as many as 10,000 people may have died in the violence, while others estimate the number of deaths at several hundred.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The majority of the deaths occurred on June 3-4, 1989, when Chinese troops and tanks were sent into Tiananmen Square to suppress the protests.
